Start with the task and action interface, then check sensing, timing, held-out splits, access and license. Dataset size alone does not establish that the data fits your robot.2Robot learning is the use of data and experience to train robots to perceive, predict, or act instead of specifying every behavior as a fixed rule. The training signal may come from demonstrations, rewards, self-supervision, simulation, human feedback, or combinations of these sources.3A useful robot-learning claim must name the robot, observations, action space, data, task, training method, evaluation split, autonomy level, and real-world trial protocol. Model size or dataset size alone does not establish physical capability.4Touch matters when success depends on hidden contact state. Observations may include cameras, depth, language, proprioception, force, torque, or tactile signals. Actions may be joint commands, end-effector motion, gripper state, trajectories, or action chunks.The loop is only as reliable as its data and evaluation. Demonstration quality, timing, calibration, resets, interventions, failed attempts, and hardware changes can all alter what the learned policy actually represents.Collect synchronized observations, robot state, actions, task context, and failure metadataTrain a policy, representation, reward model, dynamics model, or reusable foundation modelEvaluate on held-out tasks, objects, scenes, robots, sensors, or physical conditionsMeasure real-robot success, speed, recovery, force, damage, and intervention instead of only offline lossTopic 05Major learning paradigmsRobot-learning labels describe different supervision and optimization choices. Many practical systems combine several of them, so comparisons should identify the exact training and deployment role.ApproachLearning signalTypical strengthEvidence boundaryImitation learningExpert or teleoperated demonstrationsDirectly learns behaviors represented in the demonstrationsSensitive to demonstration coverage and distribution shiftReinforcement learningReward from interaction or simulationCan optimize behavior through trial and feedbackReward design, safety, sample cost, and sim-to-real transfer must be reportedOffline robot learningPreviously collected trajectoriesReuses data without new online exploration during trainingCannot assume the logged data covers every useful action or failureSelf-supervised representation learningStructure inside unlabeled or weakly labeled observationsCan create reusable visual, tactile, or multimodal featuresRepresentation scores do not automatically prove closed-loop task valueVision-language-action policyRobot trajectories paired with images and instructionsConnects task language and observations to actionsEmbodiment, action interface, data mix, and real-robot evaluation determine scopeTopic 06Data is part of the robot systemOpen X-Embodiment, DROID, and the LeRobot ecosystem illustrate different routes toward reusable robot data: cross-embodiment aggregation, a large real-world manipulation dataset, and a standardized open data and tooling ecosystem. They are complementary examples, not interchangeable benchmarks.A dataset record should expose the robot, sensor streams, control interface, task labels, trajectory unit, timing, calibration, collection policy, train-test split, access path, and license. Without those fields, scale is difficult to interpret and reuse is harder to audit.Topic 07Simulation and sim-to-real transferSimulation can generate experience, perturbations, labels, and repeatable evaluation without exposing hardware to every trial. Transfer to a physical robot still depends on geometry, dynamics, contact, sensing, latency, control, and observation differences between the simulator and the deployed system.Report what was randomized, adapted, calibrated, or fine-tuned, and separate simulation success from repeated physical trials. A simulator benchmark can test a method under controlled conditions; it does not by itself establish real-world reliability.ADEPT is a current source-bounded example: it pretrains generic object reposing in simulation, then trains each embodiment and downstream task independently before transferring student policies to two physical workbench systems without real-world fine-tuning. Its use of “zero-shot sim-to-real” does not mean zero-shot transfer to a new hand, sensor, task, or robot.SoftMimicGen adapts a small library of deformable-object demonstrations into successful simulated trajectories for policy training. Its three real-robot comparisons distinguish simulation-only and joint training; the towel result ties the real-only baseline. The source review separates generation acceptance, policy success and the RGB-D deployment pathway from untested tactile claims.SoftMimicGen: method, real-robot evidence and tactile limitsTopic 08Tactile robot learningTactile in-context learning uses examples in the model input rather than updating its parameters. Tactile-ETA pairs action segments with before-and-after camera views, robot state and tactile observations; it retains tactile endpoints and selected change frames in ordered demonstrations. The frozen agent also receives current sensing and execution feedback.In four simulated tasks, the authors keep two expert demonstrations, current inputs and the execution interface fixed. Adding tactile observations inside the demonstrations raises mean success from 15.75% to 24%, with 100 trials per task and condition; not every task improves. On Wipe Board and Pick Up Chips, each condition has current vision and touch: one aligned multimodal demonstration versus none yields 3/5 versus 0/5 successes per task. This is not a touch-versus-no-touch comparison or an industrial reliability estimate.Decisions occur between motion segments, so this context does not replace fast tactile feedback control during execution. These are author-reported results from the October 20, 2026 v1 preprint, with source and code inspection updated October 22; RoboSkin has not run the controller or reproduced the results. Task coverage and hardware samples are small.A separate Lift Bottle ablation in the same v1 holds the two demonstrations, their visual-motion content and current sensing fixed: endpoints yield 27/100 successes, all historical tactile frames 2/100, and endpoints plus a selected change pair 36/100. This supports testing action-aligned frame selection, not a general claim that dense touch is harmful. The separate TacTalent Astra study changes touch in both demonstrations and online inputs, so its modality comparison answers a different question.Touch can enter robot learning as raw tactile images, force or pressure arrays, compact contact representations, predicted future observations, a reward signal, or a fast correction pathway. The right representation depends on the sensor, task, controller rate, and data available.ManiSkill-ViTac provides a primary-source example of a simulation benchmark focused on visuo-tactile manipulation. Physical tactile datasets and full-hand benchmarks add different evidence. Results should stay attached to their robot, sensor, task, split, and protocol.UniVTAC makes those units explicit: 205,826 samples pretrain a tactile encoder, 400 paper-reported trajectories train eight task policies, the September inventory lists 800 task HDF5 files for each of Isaac Sim 4.5 and 5.1, and 450 physical demonstrations support three real-world tasks. Evaluation rollouts are outcomes rather than additional training data.In ADEPT, the tactile pathway is limited to five vision-based fingertips on one Flexiv-Sharpa student. The paper reports 3/10 vision-only versus 8/10 visuo-tactile final success in one matched insertion condition with ten trials per modality. This is useful causal evidence inside that condition, not proof of cross-sensor or cross-hand transfer.Synchronize touch with camera frames, pose, joint state, action, and contact eventsCompare against matched no-touch or shuffled-touch baselines where tactile value is claimedTest occlusion, slip, insertion, deformable objects, or disturbances that make contact information relevantReport sensor calibration, wear, drift, replacement, and latency when they can affect the learned behaviorRole of tactile dataWhat changes?What to check before reuseFine-tuningAn optimizer changes model parameters using training records.Separate training and held-out episodes; retain sensor calibration and the action contract.Demonstrations in contextExamples condition a fixed model at inference.Keep observations aligned with actions, segment order and outcomes; distinguish recorded touch from current touch.Execution feedbackNew observations inform the next decision or controller correction.Measure observation age, decision interval and actuation latency; a supplied touch stream alone does not establish a fast control loop.Tactile-ETA v1: controlled comparisons, limitations and hardware protocolCompare Tactile-ETA and the TacTalent Astra setup, with a matched frame-selection planInspect episode fields, timing and action conventionsConnect tactile feedback to manipulation outcomesScope a robot-data and integration evidence reviewTopic 09How to evaluate robot-learning claimsEvaluation should make the claimed generalization axis explicit. Its official v0.6.0 release expands policy evaluation and model-development workflows. These releases are useful infrastructure signals; any capability claim still needs the named policy, dataset, robot, task, and evaluation result.Google DeepMind’s Gemini Robotics materials represent another branch of the field: models intended to connect multimodal understanding and robot action. RoboSkin.ai keeps those broad model developments connected to the narrower question of when tactile evidence improves contact-rich behavior.Topic 11Collective experience learning: what does “without human corrections” remove?The October 19, 2026 preprint by Chao Yu, Shu’ang Yu and colleagues at Tsinghua University, AgiBot and Infinigence AI names three distinct pieces: collective experience learning (CEL), the shared-policy learning paradigm; failure-guided experience retrieval fine-tuning (FERT), its algorithm; and FATS, the fault-tolerant asynchronous training system.FERT uses observations before a failed execution ends to retrieve successful fleet segments. Their recorded actions become prioritized supervised fine-tuning targets. Compared with imitation learning from new expert demonstrations, it changes the source and selection of action supervision; it still learns by fitting successful actions.“Without additional expert corrections” applies after expert SFT and HG-DAgger initialization. Humans still label episode outcomes and reset environments. Inputs include RGB views and proprioception, not tactile skin. This is not unattended learning.The authors evaluate each policy/task over 120 trials split between two held-out AgiBot G2 robots. That tests other instances of the same platform, not cross-model transfer. Holding collection time per robot fixed gives larger fleets more total experience, so fleet size alone cannot explain the gains. These are author experiments, not RoboSkin tests. Source review: October 20, 2026, v1.Budget initial demonstrations and corrective teleoperation separately from ongoing outcome labeling, resets, maintenance and failed-run review. Ask for operator time per successful episode before estimating labor savings.Keep robot identity, policy version, outcome labels, failed-query provenance and retrieved-success provenance in the data contract. Audit retrieval quality and prevent held-out robot data from entering training.To isolate a fleet-size effect, compare equal total data or interaction budgets as well as equal time per robot. Predefine task success, intervention rules and held-out instances.CEL paper v1: FERT, human supervision and evaluation protocolLearning from Fleet Experience: paper and version historyCEL author project pageInspect the teleoperation data contractCompare VLA action interfaces and evidenceScope a research and integration evidence reviewTopic 12DexOAK: from human hand-object motion to robot referencesDexOAK (Object-Aware Kinematic Retargeting) uses structured human hand-object motion capture to produce robot wrist and joint references. Its inputs include human keypoints and object geometry, not arbitrary video or tactile sensor recordings. Contact-aware geometry is not a measured touch signal.An interaction-graph optimizer supplies training references. A learned retargeter then generates references without solving each new frame, with contact and collision objectives refining the mapping. A separate residual reinforcement-learning stage corrects dynamics; a plausible hand pose alone is not an executable trajectory.The authors report 46/56 successful open-loop replays on a UR5 with a right Allegro hand across Take out, Close gate, Pour, Unplug and Cut. They select the first successful simulation rollout per policy, then repeat it four times. Objects are manually reset near the simulated starting pose. This measures repeatability after selection, not end-to-end success over arbitrary human inputs; failed simulation policies can reduce the hardware denominator.The project page shows seven tasks: the five main-table tasks plus held-out Close Laptop and Press Button, each reported at 10/12 hardware replays. Those two use a frozen retargeter but still receive task-specific RL. The seven-task showcase and five-task 46/56 total therefore describe different sets.Reviewed October 20, 2026 against the October 19 v1 preprint and author project page. These are author experiments, not RoboSkin reproduction results. The project’s GitHub label has no repository destination and is marked pending; code, weights, release terms and runnable reproduction are unverified.For a data-conversion decision, keep a record of what each stage adds or removes. mainEntity.name: What is the difference between imitation learning and reinforcement learning for robots?

acceptedAnswer.text: Imitation learning learns from demonstrated behavior. Reinforcement learning improves behavior using a reward signal from interaction or simulation. Systems can combine both.

mainEntity.name: What makes a robot-learning dataset useful?

acceptedAnswer.text: It should identify the robot, observations, actions, task context, timing, calibration, trajectory unit, collection policy, splits, access path, and license.

mainEntity.name: Why does robot learning need tactile data?

acceptedAnswer.text: It needs tactile data when physical success depends on pressure, shear, slip, seating, deformation, or contact transitions that other sensors do not measure directly.

mainEntity.name: How should sim-to-real results be judged?

acceptedAnswer.text: State what was trained in simulation, what was randomized or adapted, which physical robot and tasks were tested, how many trials were run, and which failures or interventions occurred.

@graph.description: Robot learning data includes observations, robot state, actions, task context and outcomes used to train or evaluate a robot model. Start with the task and action interface, then check sensing, timing, held-out splits, access and license. Dataset size alone does not establish that the data fits your robot. Robot learning is the use of data and experience to train robots to perceive, predict, or act instead of specifying every behavior as a fixed rule. The training signal may come from demonstrations, rewards, self-supervision, simulation, human feedback, or combinations of these sources. A useful robot-learning claim must name the robot, observations, action space, data, task, training method, evaluation split, autonomy level, and real-world trial protocol. Model size or dataset size alone does not establish physical capability. Touch matters when success depends on hidden contact state. Tactile observations can expose pressure, shear, slip, seating, deformation, and contact transitions that vision and proprioception may not measure directly.

To use it for learning, document the action interface, align clocks, retain resets and interventions, check episode quality, and define evaluation splits and reuse terms. Teleoperation demonstrates human control, not autonomous policy capability.2Robot teleoperation is remote or mediated human control of a robot through interfaces such as joysticks, teach pendants, motion capture, wearable devices, cameras, handheld end effectors, or bilateral systems. Teleoperated behavior is not autonomous behavior.3For robot learning, teleoperation can generate aligned observations and actions, but useful data also requires calibration, timing, task definitions, resets, failures, operator context, quality control, schema, access, and license.4Demonstrations do not become a capable policy automatically. Training must account for action representation, embodiment, coverage, compounding errors, evaluation splits, interventions, and repeated real-robot testing.Topic 01Trace the action target before collecting or converting dataA field named action is not a complete control specification. Trace one record through its producing software and training loader to the intended robot interface. Dimension, units, reference frame, absolute versus incremental meaning, rotation representation and observation-to-action timing all belong in that record.DROID provides a concrete source-inspected example. Its public schema lists a seven-element action and several action_dict fields. The pinned policy-learning example instead constructs a ten-element target: three Cartesian-position values, six values representing rotation, and one gripper position. It marks these targets absolute and leaves the gripper dimension out of normalization. This is a particular training pipeline, not a claim that every DROID user has the same target.EvidenceWhat the inspected material saysWhat to do with itDROID serialized schemaSeven-element action; separate commanded Cartesian/joint position and velocity fields, plus observed state.Record the exact raw field. The docs’ short “6x joint velocities” comment is insufficient to specify a controller and is not used here as a verified joint-action contract.DROID pinned transformdroid_dataset_transform builds 3 + 6 + 1 values from action_dict.cartesian_position and gripper_position.Pin the transform and normalization. A ten-element rotation representation cannot be sent as ten robot joint commands.DROID pinned loaderThe example selects two exterior cameras and filters for success trajectories by default. A later transform slices action[1:] within its prepared window.Inspect camera selection, filtering and temporal alignment in the actual training recipe; source inspection alone does not validate a loaded batch.Tactile-ETA released demonstrationsMeasured end-effector/joint transitions and recorded simulation steps; original actuator/tool commands are marked unavailable.Useful for historical context; do not relabel measured displacement as the original control command.A practical collection checkpointBefore a larger collection session, complete the action-contract sheet and replay a small pilot batch through the intended loader. Retain a visible success, a failure or intervention, and a missing/stale-data case where available. Keep attempts and exclusions in the ledger; do not collect only a polished demonstration video.Define acceptance thresholds from the target robot and task, then record who checked them and what is still unresolved. This is an engineering planning aid, not a safety certification or a claim that RoboSkin has tested your controller. The DROID findings above are source inspection on October 28, 2026; no DROID training or hardware run was performed.DROID official data schemaPinned DROID target construction, lines 27–38Pinned DROID loader and camera/filter settingsTactile-ETA preparation: recorded motion and unavailable commandsDownload the action-contract sheet (CSV)Download the complete decision kit with instructionsChoose an existing dataset before scaling new collectionTopic 02Robot teleoperation data collection: episode-quality checklistDefine the learning data contract before choosing an interface. Direct robot teleoperation can record commands for a particular embodiment; original UMI instead uses an instrumented handheld gripper and reconstructs trajectories for later policy deployment. Neither raw video nor a controller joint angle is automatically a calibrated tactile measurement.Review a small set of recorded episodes before scaling collection. Inspect the streams together, preserve failures and corrections, and document what was commanded versus what the robot measured. Passing file validation alone does not show that the resulting policy succeeds on a physical robot.Collection checkWhat the episode should documentWhat to verifyAction meaningCommand and measured state, control mode, units, frames, gripper range and retargeting.The targets match the policy and deployment controller.Clock alignmentObservation, state, command and optional tactile timestamps with capture-rate metadata.Replay exposes missing frames, offsets and stale sensor values.Task coverageTask label, objects, setup, resets, failures, interventions and operator context.The retained episodes represent the conditions the policy will face.Contact evidenceSensor identity, placement, calibration and raw versus inferred touch fields.An added tactile channel is valid, synchronized and supported by the learning method.Release and evaluationDataset version, access, license and held-out split definition.The release can be used for your purpose without leaking repeated episodes into evaluation.Compare the original UMI and GELLO collection systemsValidate LeRobot fields, timestamps and conversionChoose existing robot learning data before collecting moreTopic 03Passive observation vs teleoperation data for robot learningPassive observation data can show what a human did and how a scene changed. Teleoperation can additionally record the commands sent to a particular robot alongside its measured state. That observation-action pairing is the key distinction for policy training: ordinary video does not directly tell you which robot command produced each transition.These are complementary data sources. R3M pretrains visual representations on Ego4D human video and uses the representation for downstream robot policy learning. It does not make the original videos a dataset of measured robot actions. The R3M paper is an example of representation pretraining followed by task learning, not proof that every imitation-learning recipe can train from unlabelled video.UMI is a third case: an instrumented handheld demonstration interface. Its gripper-mounted camera and trajectory-processing pipeline provide more structure than passive video, while collection can happen away from a robot. GELLO instead controls a robot through a joint-based interface. Record additional calibrated sensing if the task needs it.Teleoperation with added tactile sensingAligned commands, measured state and recorded touch; haptic feedback to the operator is an independent design choice.A suitable robot, interface and tactile sensor with a documented capture pipeline.Preserve raw units, calibration, validity and clocks. A recorded tactile channel does not prove a trained policy uses it.R3M: visual pretraining from human videoUMI: demonstration and policy interfaceGELLO: joint-based teleoperation designTopic 04Choose data by the training taskFor visual representation learning, video may be useful before robot action labels are available. For supervised action imitation, first establish the action representation and its alignment with observations. For contact-sensitive insertion or grasp adjustment, decide whether touch supplies an observation, a training label, operator feedback or an evaluation signal; each role requires different records.Consider inserting a plug. A passive clip shows motion and visible outcome. A teleoperation log can also preserve the commanded motion and measured robot state. Tactile sensing can add a local contact observation when the camera cannot see the mating surfaces. To compare these sources, hold out objects or scenes, report autonomous success separately from intervention, and state which streams the deployed policy actually receives. The operator may watch direct video, stereo or depth views, a digital twin, or the physical robot. Some systems provide haptic or force feedback; others are one-way.The interface changes the data. It does not prove that a learned policy can perceive the same state, recover from error, or act safely without the operator.A policy trained by imitation can encounter states absent from expert demonstrations because small prediction errors compound during execution. Corrective demonstrations, interactive data collection, recovery examples, and policy rollouts can target this gap, but they still require an explicit intervention policy and fair evaluation.Topic 08Current open data-collection signalsThe official Hugging Face Grabette article describes a handheld gripper-and-camera device that records data in the standard LeRobot dataset format. It is an example of collecting manipulation demonstrations without keeping a full robot in the loop during every recording. The transfer value still depends on calibration, task coverage, observation and action mapping, and later robot evaluation.The LeRobot v0.6 release describes rollout tools and DAgger-style human corrections. Robot-side tactile data can label contact onset, slip, pressure distribution, or grasp state. mainEntity.name: Can passive video replace teleoperation data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Passive video can support representation learning, but it does not directly supply synchronized robot action targets. Using it for policy learning requires a suitable learning objective, inferred or additional action information, and evaluation on the target robot.

mainEntity.name: Is UMI the same as passive video collection?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Original UMI uses an instrumented handheld gripper and a trajectory-processing pipeline to provide a structured demonstration and policy interface. It can collect away from a robot, but its original design does not include a default calibrated tactile or force stream.

Robot teleoperation is remote or mediated human control of a robot through an interface such as a joystick, teach pendant, motion-capture system, wearable device, handheld end effector, or bilateral master.
No. Teleoperation shows human-controlled behavior. Autonomous capability requires the robot policy to perceive and act without the operator under a defined evaluation protocol.

mainEntity.name: How does teleoperation create robot-learning data?

acceptedAnswer.text: It records synchronized observations, robot state, human commands, actions, task context, and outcomes. Those episodes are calibrated, quality-checked, normalized, split, and used to train and evaluate a policy.
Limits include interface bias, latency, morphology mismatch, narrow task coverage, inconsistent operators, missing failures, action retargeting, compounding policy errors, and evaluation leakage.

mainEntity.name: Why record tactile data during teleoperation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Touch can expose contact onset, pressure, shear, slip, seating, and corrective behavior that cameras may miss, but it must be synchronized with robot state and actions to support learning.

audit of 24 demonstration segments.Published 2026-10-22 | Updated 2026-10-28 by RoboSkin.ai Editorial TeamOctober 28, 2026: added a reproducible offline audit of two pinned Lift Bottle demonstrations, 24 action segments and 96 published image strips, plus a versioned experiment kit. Paper results retain the October 22 source review. RoboSkin has not run either controller or the proposed A/B/C task-success experiment.Inspect the executed input auditBrowse researchSubmit a sourceTechnology visual showing tactile sensing layers and signal flow.Compare the evidence or check the inputsCompare methods and action interfacesSee what each setup receives, changes and executes.Inspect the executed input auditCheck observed counts, pixel agreement, source revisions and limits.Plan a matched A/B/C experimentDownload code, the report and blank outcome records.On this pageWhat is actually being compared?Simulation: what Tactile-ETA’s controlled comparison showsSimulation: what the TacTalent Astra study reportsReal robots: ten trials per condition, across two tasksMore tactile frames are not necessarily betterExecuted input audit: what the released Lift Bottle files containNext experiment: matched tasks, matched vision, three tactile contextsHow to use and cite this comparisonShort answerWhat you need to know1Tactile-ETA and TacTalent both use GPT-6 Astra, with different context and control designs. Tactile-ETA supplies action-aligned tactile demonstrations and robot tools to a frozen agent. TacTalent uses Astra with RoboICL to generate action sequences from scene images, tactile images and demonstration context. Compare these configured systems, not the model name alone.2Tactile-ETA isolates the value of adding touch to the same two demonstrations: mean simulation success rises from 15.75% to 24.00% across four tasks. TacTalent reports 93.8% on UniVTAC and 81.8% on OpenViTac with vision and touch, under a different evaluation. These percentages do not establish a winner between the two setups.3The hardware evidence is much smaller: Tactile-ETA reports 6/10 successes with one multimodal demonstration per task versus 0/10 without demonstrations, pooled across two tasks. Both conditions receive current touch. TacTalent reports simulation only. The next useful experiment is a matched comparison of endpoints, endpoints plus peak-change frames, and complete tactile sequences.4RoboSkin independently checked the released inputs for two Lift Bottle episodes: 24 action segments, 96 image strips and 228 panels matched the raw data. This is an offline input audit, not a reproduction of robot success. The script, full report and experiment records are available below.Topic 01What is actually being compared?In-context learning conditions a model through examples supplied at inference; it does not mean updating model weights. The useful comparison is between two ways to package experience and connect a general model to a robot. Neither study establishes that an unconfigured chat model can control arbitrary hardware.Tactile-ETA’s main configuration identifies gpt-6-astra with low reasoning effort. TacTalent’s method configuration identifies gpt-6-astra with xhigh effort. Shared model naming therefore does not imply matched inference settings, camera inputs, prompts, action budgets or execution code.For the distinction between training, demonstrations and execution feedback, see the robot learning guide.DimensionTactile-ETATacTalent: Astra direct tactile-image controlCurrent inputsIn simulation: task text, head/wrist camera observations, bilateral touch, robot state and tool execution feedback. The hardware study uses wrist and third-person cameras.Task text, configured scene cameras, end-effector/proprioceptive state and, in V+T mode, two fingertip tactile RGB images. Wrist-camera availability depends on the task.Demonstration formatComplete expert episodes split at action boundaries. mainEntity.name: Is Tactile-ETA an alternative model to GPT-6 Astra?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Its main evaluated setup uses GPT-6 Astra as the frozen agent. This page compares Tactile-ETA’s context and tool design with the separate TacTalent study’s Astra/RoboICL control setup, not two independent model families.

mainEntity.name: Do the reported percentages show which setup is better?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Task sets, cameras, demonstrations, reasoning effort, scene samples and execution interfaces differ. Tactile-ETA’s 15.75% to 24.00% result is a within-study demonstration-touch comparison; TacTalent’s 93.8% and 81.8% are separate simulation suite means.

mainEntity.name: What does Tactile-ETA’s ten-trial hardware result mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each condition has five Wipe Board and five Pick Up Chips trials. One multimodal demonstration per task yields 6/10 combined successes versus 0/10 without demonstrations. Both conditions have current touch. This small sample does not establish deployment reliability or isolate historical touch from the rest of the demonstration.

mainEntity.name: Should a robot agent always receive fewer tactile frames?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Tactile-ETA reports 2/100 for all demonstration frames and 36/100 for its selected representation on Lift Bottle, under one fixed setup. Test endpoints, endpoints plus a peak-change pair and full sequences under matched conditions before generalizing.
